title: potentilla glandulosa subsp. nevadensis
intro: Potentilla glandulosa subsp. nevadensis, commonly known as the Sierra cinquefoil or Five-Fingers, is a plant species in the rose family (Rosaceae) that is native to the mountainous regions of western North America. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which may help to reduce pain and inflammation, and protect against cell damage. The therapeutic actions of Potentilla glandulosa subsp. nevadensis include its ability to exhibit immunomodulatory and antimicrobial activities, making it a potential treatment for various infections and conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and alkaloids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
